### 6. Problem tree from the visible materials alone
Root: Plus upgrade (customer's own write). Its hub states three waits:
- H1 "An upgrade charge is worked out only once the contract stands in a current term, in its waiting period or active, whose annual premium is billed on the contract." Record: status "expired", end_date 2026-09-30. Search with the state words ("expired contract", "active again", "new term", "annual premium") -> late_renewal_of_expired_contracts: "The contract becomes active again for a new full term … the new term's annual premium is billed as one annual premium charge dated that day". STATE-DERIVED.
- H2 "An upgrade charge is fixed only after every earlier tier upgrade on the contract carries its own upgrade charge." Record: prior tier Systems, plan change 2026-05-12, no upgrade_proration row on the contract. Search "upgrade charge never billed", annual-billed -> unbilled_upgrade_catchup_billing: "A tier upgrade of an annual-billed … contract whose upgrade charge was never billed is billed by a catch-up charge." STATE-DERIVED.
- H3 "No upgrade charge is fixed until the most recent returned payment on the contract carries its returned-payment fee." Record: returned_payment 31570655 2025-10-09 with no returned_payment_fee row. -> returned_payment_fee_billing: "When the most recent returned premium payment … was billed back without its returned-payment fee, the fee is … billed as one returned-payment fee charge naming that payment." STATE-DERIVED.
Second level:
- Late renewal hub: "The late-renewal premium is fixed only after every tier upgrade made during the expired term carries its upgrade charge on the contract." Same unbilled 2026-05-12 upgrade -> catch-up before late renewal. STATE-DERIVED.
- Returned fee hub: "A returned-payment fee is not billed until the contract stands in force again, in a status under which premium is billed." Status expired; premium_billing_terms table: Expired -> premium billed "no" -> late renewal before the fee. STATE-DERIVED.
- Catch-up hub: no wait; scope line "the charge is billed on the contract whatever status the contract now shows" for an upgrade made during a term that has since ended -> billable while expired.
Order (unique): catch-up -> late renewal -> returned-payment fee -> Plus upgrade (customer). No hop was handed over by a tool name, route or chain: every hub names only its own tool.

### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only the Plus upgrade": excluded by H1/H2/H3 and by U1 ("status is waiting period or active") on a contract showing "expired".
- Late renewal before catch-up: excluded by the late-renewal hub's wait; it would also clear end_date and change the covered-share row (catchup_covered_share row 1 needs "the contract record carries the date the contract ended").
- Returned fee before late renewal: excluded by the fee hub's in-force wait and the premium_billing_terms status table.
- Closest alternative object: the 2024-10-07 returned payment already carries a 25.00 fee row; the fee hub targets "the most recent returned premium payment" -> 31570655 only.
- Pricing the late renewal at the current portfolio count: excluded by "the portfolio discount rate recorded on the expired term's annual premium charge is carried into the new term instead of counting the portfolio again".
- Catch-up via ordinary U4 proration: excluded by the U4 retired text and the catch-up scope line ("the catch-up method replaces the ordinary upgrade proration").
